problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}$, where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 57\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+2\cdot 0+57\cdot 7}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{7}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1+399}{1+49} \\  & =\frac{400}{50} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}=\frac{8}{2}=4.
$$
